Respondent No.1 Food and Safety Officer of the BBMP North Zone, filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. alleging that, on 12.3.2021, he visited a shop, in which the milk produced by the petitioner herein stacked for selling to the general public.
The Milk which was produced by the petitioner was seized and sent to the food analyst for examination on 12.3.2021.

The Food analyst submitted a report on 12.3.2021 stating that the milk produced by the petitioner is unsafe as per the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "Act, 2006")
2.
The learned Magistrate after perusing the complaint took cognizance of the offence punishable under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Taking exception of the same, this petition is filed.

3. Mr. Dhyan Chinnappa, learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner is the Managing Director of the Tirumala Milks Products Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Indian Companies Act, 1956, which is the purchaser of the milk in question, and the company having not been arrayed as an accused, the petitioner cannot be vicariously held guilty as specified under section 66 of the Act, 2006.

He further submits that the milk which was NC:
2023:KHC:40241 seized from the shop was wrapped in Brown paper cover and thereafter sent to the food analyst for examination, therefore, the food inspector has not taken sufficient precaution in sending the milk to the food analyst.
4. Respondent No. 2 is served with notice and has not chosen to appear in person or through his counsel.

5. Considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
6. Admittedly, the subject milk was produced by the Tirumala Milks Products Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Indian Companies Act, 1956. Section 66 of the Act, 2006 deals Managing Director vs Food Safety Officer on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185605802/
2 with the offences by the companies which specifies that when the offence committed is by a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company,
shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, if a person commits the offence as a Director of the company he along with the company shall also be held guilty.
7. The company having not been arrayed as an accused, the petitioner who is the managing director of the company cannot be held vicariously guilty as stated section 66 of the Act, 2006.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:40241 ORDER i) The criminal petition is allowed ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.110/2021 pending on the file of the Special Court for Economic Offences, Bengaluru, insofar it relates to the petitioner herein stands quashed.
